newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Palestinians urge U.N. sanctions against Israel.
newsitem.headline: Palestinians urge U.N. sanctions against Israel.

text.p: Palestinians urged the United Nations on Thursday to consider imposing economic sanctions on Israel ahead of a U.N. debate over a new Jewish settlement in Jerusalem that has frozen peace moves.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu meanwhile vowed to tighten the Jewish state's grip on the holy city.

Ahmed Abdel-Rahman, general secretary of Palestinian President Yasser Arafat's cabinet, said Israel must halt construction of the Har Homa Jewish settlement begun last month on a hilltop known in Arabic as Jabal Abu Ghneim.

"In this time of Netanyahu's government the use of the word pressure and the imposition of sanctions on Israel should not be forbidden any more but it has to become a necessity for the peace process," he told Reuters on Thursday.

"If Israel refuses to be committed to the peace process, to implement signed agreements, we think that economic sanctions should be imposed on Israel as happened with some countries that violated international standards as in South Africa and the former Yugoslavia," Abdel-Rahman said.

The 185-member U.N. General Assembly, holding only its 10th emergency special session in 47 years, is due to consider whether countries should bar assistance to Israeli private and public establishments involved in Jewish settlement. The assembly's decisions are not binding.
The expected two-day debate was prompted by construction of 6,500 homes for Jews begun last month at the site on the outskirts of Arab East Jerusalem.
On Wednesday night Netanyahu, whose right-wing government came to power in June last year, insisted on a right to build for Jews in any part of the city which Israel views as its "eternal" capital.
"We are building in Jerusalem, in all parts of Jerusalem, and we will go on building in Jerusalem," Netanyahu told thousands of cheering ultra-nationalist religious supporters at a Jerusalem stadium.

Appearing in a skullcap worn by religious Jews, Netanyahu invoked the biblical names of the West Bank telling the crowd: "Together we will maintain the Jewish settlements in Judea, Samaria and the Gaza Strip."

Israel captured East Jerusalem in the 1967 Middle East war and annexed it. Palestinians view it as the capital of a hoped-for state and condemn the settlement as an Israeli attempt to pre-empt negotiations on the future of the city due to be completed by May 1999.

The United States used its veto twice last month to block U.N. Security Council resolutions calling on Israel to abandon the widely criticised settlement which sparked an outburst of violence in the West Bank and Gaza Strip.

Washington, the main broker in Middle East peacemaking, criticised Israel's action during the debates but said Israelis and Palestinians should resolve the issues in negotiations -- not at the United Nations.

Under the draft proposal, still subject to change, U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan would be asked to monitor the situation via a team of U.N. observers and to submit a report within two months of the resolution's adoption.
